JPM.rationale: JPMorgan Chase demonstrates strong fundamental health with accelerating earnings trajectory: Q1 2026 revenue of $49.84B (+10% YoY) and EPS of $5.94 (+17.2% YoY) represent the strongest quarterly performance in the available history. Net income of $16.49B was a record, with markets revenue up 20% and investment banking fees jumping 28%. The bank maintains industry-leading profitability with 16.2% ROE and 39.9% operating margins, supported by a diversified business model across consumer banking, investment banking, and asset management. Balance sheet remains robust with $364B in equity against $4.9T in assets. Valuation is moderately attractive: current P/E of 15.02x sits near the lower end of its 13.7-17.8x 365-day range, while P/B of 2.43x is below the 2.8x peak. The stock has recovered +12.9% over the past quarter but remains below its 52-week high of $338.09. Near-term catalyst exists with Q2 2026 earnings on July 14, where consensus expects EPS of $5.42 (+9.7% YoY), and the bank's 7% NII growth target has become more achievable given the higher-for-longer rate environment with Fed funds at 3.63%. However, risks temper the score: CEO Dimon flagged expenses potentially reaching $106B (above prior $105B guidance), DOJ subpoenas over 'debanking' practices add regulatory uncertainty, and nonperforming exposure rose 11% with nonaccrual loans surging 53% in Q1. The T10Y2Y spread has compressed to 0.27% (from 0.49% in late March), signaling potential curve flattening headwinds for NIM.
